The auditor should be explicitly instructed to map 'foreflippers' to 'forelimbs' and 'hind flippers' to 'hindlimbs' to ensure keypoint detection logic applies correctly.

audited_plan.image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a sea lion resting on a rocky surface. The animal is lying on its side with its head resting near its foreflipper. The fur is golden-brown, appearing wet or sleek. Visible features include the head, closed eye, whiskers, external ear flap, and one large foreflipper tucked against the body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad with prominent sagittal crest in males.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape appears relatively smooth and rounded without the distinct, bony protrusion of a sagittal crest typical of mature male sea lions. It resembles a female or juvenile morphology more than a dominant male.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: External ear pinnae (visible ear flaps) distinguish from true seals.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A small, distinct external ear flap is clearly visible on the side of the head, confirming it is an otariid (eared seal/sea lion) and not a phocid (true seal).
Long, light-colored whiskers are clearly visible extending from the muzzle area.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Fur is short and coarse ranging from brown to dark grey, lighter on ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fur texture appears short and sleek (consistent with wet fur), and the color is a uniform golden-brown. While the ventral surface isn't fully exposed, the visible tone matches the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body exhibits streamlined fusiform form of substantial marine mammal proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible torso section shows the characteristic thick, tapering body shape of a pinniped.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Males develop thick neck mane and are significantly larger than females.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is no visible thick mane of longer hair around the neck; the transition from head to body is smooth, suggesting this is likely a female or immature male.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Foreflippers are large, broad, and hairless on underside used for terrestrial locomotion.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large foreflipper is prominently displayed in the foreground. It appears broad and the visible skin texture suggests the leathery, hairless quality typical of the underside/palm.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Hind flippers can rotate forward for walking on land.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The hind flippers are completely occluded by the body position and the rock; they are not visible in the frame.
Due to the recumbent pose and camera angle, only one side of the body is clearly visible, making symmetry verification impossible.
